summary: Scope-limited production connection metrics harvest for privacy assessment
description: Issue summary: Customer privacy team has requested a scoped export of connection-level production metrics to validate an internal privacy posture for telemetry retention. Impact: The extract is for internal compliance assessment only; no customer-visible outages expected but this touches sensitive request/connection identifiers and must be minimized. Environment: Production (us-west cluster), metrics and lightweight traces only; not request payloads or inference outputs. Requested fields: connection_id (hashed), timestamp, model_id, route, request_size_bytes, response_size_bytes, duration_ms, upstream_region. Excluded fields: any raw prompt text, kv-cache content, or PII fields. Duration: one-time export covering a rolling 72-hour window ending 2026-03-09 23:59 UTC. Justification: Privacy team needs concrete sample metrics to test redaction heuristics and retention policy tooling. Approvals required: Security (SRE-Security), Privacy (Legal-Privacy), Observability lead. Access model: timeboxed, read-only export of aggregated/hashed identifiers; data will be stored in an ephemeral S3 bucket with enforced lifecycle (7 days) and restricted IAM principals only. Minimization plan: connection_id will be HMAC-shifted with a per-run salt and stored as hex digest; no IP addresses or customer user IDs will be included. Deliverables: CSV with column descriptions, redaction proof (hash verification script), and deletion confirmation. Steps to produce extract: 1) Create a scoped query on metrics DB (metrics-store/analytics) for the desired 72-hour window. 2) Apply transformation lambda to HMAC-connection_id and drop excluded columns. 3) Write to pre-provisioned encrypted S3 bucket with limited ACL. 4) Share temporary S3 presigned link with privacy + security. 5) Run deletion job and post deletion verification steps. Risk mitigations: pre-run dry-run on staging with synthetic data; approvals and audit logging; include an automatic deletion marker and confirm via S3 access logs. Contact points: Aisha Patel (reporter), Marco Chen (assignee), Priya Nair (Privacy), Jordan Miles (SRE-Security).
steps_to_reproduce: Not applicable (data extraction request). Operational steps are in 'description' and will be executed via infra runbook. Key reproducible check is running the transformation script on staging aggregates to validate no payload leakage.
logs_snippets: No raw request logs included. Example transformed row: "conn_hmac: 7ac9f3e4..., timestamp: 2026-03-08T12:34:56Z, model_id: redwood-v1-small, route: /v1/generate, req_bytes: 1024, resp_bytes: 2048, duration_ms: 132"
investigation_notes: Initial discovery: Privacy team requested representative metrics to evaluate retention defaults. Observability team confirmed metrics-store query exists and can be limited to connection-level aggregates. SRE-Security raised concern about potential accidental inclusion of IPs in older columns; audit of schema performed and flagged legacy 'client_addr' column which will be explicitly excluded. Staging dry-run passed with synthetic data and HMAC salt rotation. Access policy drafted to only permit role 'privacy-data-reviewer' for the operation.
